      - heading "Understand Angle in a Semicircle" [level=2]
  - text: CLASS 10 · CIRCLE PROOFS
  - heading "Angle in a Semicircle" [level=1]
  - paragraph: The angle subtended by a diameter at any point on the circle is a right angle (90°).
  - text: 24 min INTERMEDIATE VISUAL EXPLORATION NCERT 10.2 Geometry
  - navigation:
    - button "Interact"
    - button "Learn"
    - button "Example"
    - button "Formula"
    - button "Practice"
  - main:
    - complementary:
      - heading "DRAG & EXPLORE" [level=2]
      - paragraph: Drag point C anywhere on the semicircle.
      - strong: "Result: ∠ACB is always 90°."
      - heading "Measurements" [level=3]
      - term: ∠ACB (at C)
      - definition: 90.00°
      - term: ∠CAB (at A)
      - definition: 34.00°
      - term: ∠CBA (at B)
      - definition: 56.00°
      - heading "Lengths" [level=3]
      - paragraph: AC = 7.06 BC = 10.46 AB (diameter) = 12.62
      - paragraph: AC² + BC² = 49.8 + 109.46 = 159.26
      - paragraph: AB² = 12.62² = 159.26
      - img
      - text: Right triangle verified! AC² + BC² = AB²
    - article:
      - img "Angle in a semicircle interactive diagram":
        - text: Chord Tangent Angle
        - slider "Point C on semicircle"
        - text: A (−6.31, 0) B (6.31, 0) C (2.36, 5.85) O (0, 0) 34.00° 56.00° 90.00°
      - text: "Triangle ACB Radii: OA, OB, OC Circle (radius OA)"
    - text: Animation
    - button "Start auto-drag":
      - img
    - text: Auto-drag C
    - slider "Point C position": "68"
    - button "Slow"
    - button "Medium"
    - button "Fast"
    - button "Reset":
      - img
      - text: Reset
    - article:
      - heading "WHY IT WORKS (PROOF IDEA)" [level=2]
      - list:
        - listitem: Join OC. Since OA = OC and OB = OC, triangles AOC and BOC are isosceles.
        - listitem: Let ∠CAO = ∠ACO = α and ∠CBO = ∠OCB = β.
        - listitem: Angles around O give 2(α + β) = 180°.
        - listitem: Therefore α + β = 90°.
      - strong:
        - img
        - text: Therefore, ∠ACB = 90°.
    - article:
      - heading "WORKED EXAMPLE" [level=2]
      - paragraph: "Given: Circle with centre O(0,0), radius 7. Diameter AB with A(−7,0), B(7,0)."
      - text: C A O B
      - paragraph: ∠ACB = 90.00° ∠CAB + ∠CBA = 90.00°
      - text: "Check: AC² + BC² = AB² ✓"
    - article:
      - heading "DON’T GET TRICKED!" [level=2]:
        - img
        - text: DON’T GET TRICKED!
      - paragraph: If AB is not a diameter (just a chord), ∠ACB is not 90°.
      - paragraph: The right angle happens only when AB is a diameter.
      - strong: "Rule: Must be a diameter."
    - article:
      - heading "YOUR CHALLENGE" [level=2]
      - paragraph: Drag point C around the semicircle and try to keep ∠ACB = 90°.
      - text: Target 90° Current 90.00°
      - emphasis: Great! You nailed it.
    - article:
      - heading "WHAT YOU DISCOVERED" [level=2]
      - paragraph:
        - img
        - text: For any point C on the semicircle with diameter AB, ∠ACB is always 90°.
      - paragraph:
        - img
        - text: This is the Angle in a Semicircle theorem.
      - paragraph:
        - img
        - text: The result follows from both circle geometry and Pythagoras.
